content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors propose a method for imbalanced semi-supervised classification problems. To this end, they first use Class-Aware Pseudo-label thresholding in order to deal with imbalance within unlabeled data, and Class-Aware loss function to handle imbalance within both labeled and unlabeled data. Finally, the authors employ an extra auxiliary balanced classifier for improving accuracy more.   Unfortunately, there is no novelty at all and the authors just take all the concepts from the published papers and combine them. As a result, they obtain better accuracies on a simple Cifar-10 dataset.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
I do not see any strength in the paper since all the claimed novelties come from the existing papers. The authors present the method as a novel method, but they directly take all three techniques directly from the literature. Therefore, this is a kind of plagiarism. The authors cite the papers but they do not indicate that they use exact loss functions.  More precisely, the first contribution so called Class-aware Pseudo-Label thresholding is directly taken from the paper [1]. The authors just introduce \gamma_c term in Eq (7), but it is not a significant contribution at all. There was not any detailed explanation on the loss terms, the authors only cited [1] as a method that introduces non-linear mapping function. Therefore I checked the reference [1], and the formulations are identical with the exception of \gamma_c term, which is unacceptable. This term is defined as a hyper-parameter that must be set by the user, but there is no explanation why this term is needed.
Regarding the Class-Aware loss adjustment, the loss functions used for this goal comes from [2]. Again it is exactly the same loss function, nothing is new. Lastly, auxiliary balanced classifier is propsed by [3], and the authors do not introduce any novelty related to it.
Overall, there is no novel concept in the paper, and all claimed novelties come from the existing methods.

Also, experiments conducted on Cifar-10 is not enough to verify that these combined method outperform other methods where the main ideas come from.

Minor Issues:
The definitions given for class imbalances on page 4 are wrong. The authors divide the number of samples in class 1 with n_c. There are two mistakes: First, why to use number of samples in the first class (this does not make any sense if the number of samples of classes are sorted)?  Second, c is just an index that changes between 1 and C. So, the result will not be a value.
References
[1] Bowen Zhang, Yidong Wang, Wenxin Hou, Hao Wu, Jindong Wang, Manabu Okumura, and Takahiro Shinozaki. Flexmatch: Boosting semi-supervised learning with curriculum pseudo labeling. In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34, 2021.
[2] Aditya Krishna Menon, Sadeep Jayasumana, Ankit Singh Rawat, Himanshu Jain, Andreas Veit, and Sanjiv Kumar. Long-tail learning via logit adjustment. In 9th International Conference on Learning Representations, ICLR 2021, Virtual Event, Austria, May 3-7, 2021, 2021. 
[3] Hyuck Lee, Seungjae Shin, and Heeyoung Kim. ABC: auxiliary balanced classifier for classimbalanced semi-supervised learning. In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34: Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems 2021, NeurIPS 2021, 2021.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: All concepts are taken from the existing methods and they are not explained properly. They are better explained in the papers where they are actually introduced first. Therefore, the quality of and novelty of the paper are both low. Experiments can be reproduced provided that the authors share the codes.
content.summary_of_the_review: this is paper with no novelty. The authors merely take the 3 known concepts from the existing methods and combine them for better accuracies. However, the loss terms are not defined properly. To understand them, the reader has to read the original papers that actually propose them. This paper must be definitely rejected since the authors pretend them they propose new concepts.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper solves the semi-supervised learning under class imbalanced settings. This paper combines three techniques including Class-Aware Pseudo-label Thresholding (CAPT), Class-Aware Loss Adjustment (CALA), and Extra Auxiliary Balanced Classifier (EABC). The proposed algorithm could surpass the SOTA methods on CIFAR-10 and SVHN benchmarks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:

1.The experimental results on CIFAR-10 and SVHN show significant improvements than compared methods, especially the tail-class accuracy in Table 1, and Table 2.

Cons:

1. The first technique, i.e., Class-Aware Pseudo-label Thresholding (CAPT), is already proposed in the work of ICML 2022 [1]. However, this paper does not cite this work. Additionally, some sections are very similar to the work in ICML 2022 [1], which could raise ethic problems. The notation $\tau_c$ in Equation (6) is not defined. The hyperparameters $\gamma_c$ for classes are not explained well. For example, how to set these hyperparameters. 

2. The second technique, i.e., Class-Aware Loss Adjustment (CALA), is a commonly utilized technique to solve imbalanced data. This is not novel. Additionally, the loss function in Equation (9) is not correct. In this paper, $f_y(x:\theta)$ denotes the probability after softmax, while other works use this notation to denote the "logits". Hence, the loss is named "logit" adjustment. However, this paper directly cites other works' notations without modification, making the Equation (9) incorrect. Similarly, the denominator in Equation (5) equals 1, which could be omitted.

3. The third technique, i.e., Extra Auxiliary Balanced Classifier (EABC), also does not show any novelty. The loss of ``eabc" in Equation (16) is not defined.

[1] Class-Imbalanced Semi-Supervised Learning with Adaptive Thresholding. ICML 2022.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors propose a method called Adaptive Pseudo-labeling and Loss Adjustment (APLA) for class-imbalanced semi-supervised learning (CISSL), which includes Class-Aware Pseudo-label Thresholding (CAPT) that can utilize the imbalanced unlabeled data by dynamically adjusting the threshold for selecting pseudo-labels, and Class-Aware Loss Adjustment (CALA) that can mitigate the bias in both supervised loss and unsupervised loss.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- The proposed method is easy to understand.

Weakness
- The problem definition of this paper is unclear. In the introduction, the authors only mention the importance of the imbalanced semi-supervised learning problem itself, However, they didn’t explain what the problem of the existing solutions is that this work trying to address.
- The proposed method also lacks novelty. For example, in CAPT, the adaptive thresholding for the fixmatch based framework has already been studied [1,2]. Compared with the existing approaches, the authors should discuss the significance of the proposed method. Also, in CALA, the loss function in Eqn. (9) is just the logit adjustment which is already popular in long-tailed recognition literature. The authors should discuss on what is the difference from the existing logit adjustment loss formulation.
- The experiments are also weak. For example, the authors didn’t even evaluate their method on the CIFAR100-LT dataset which is the popular setting in imbalanced semi-supervised learning works. Of course, they didn’t evaluate their method on ImageNet or iNaturalist datasets.
- Missing reference. They didn’t compare with recent imbalanced semi-supervised learning works [1,2] neither theoretically nor empirically.

[1] DASO: Distribution-Aware Semantics-Oriented Pseudo-label for Imbalanced Semi-Supervised Learning. CVPR 2022.

[2] Class-Imbalanced Semi-Supervised Learning with Adaptive Thresholding. ICML 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The proposed method is clear, but the problem definition is not clear enough. Also, I have concerns about the novelty of the proposed method.
content.summary_of_the_review: The problem definition of this paper is not clear, and the proposed method lacks novelty. This paper also lacks a comprehensive empirical analysis of the proposed method.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
